1989-2000.what: Ground-floor windows replaced by a blank shop-front panel under a new fascia, with a wider awning; the house became a shop
1989-2000.why: Change of use from dwelling to shop

1989-2000.what: A dark rectangular box or hatch appears on the front above the awning at the upper right
1989-2000.why: Looks like a shop sign board or a blocked opening, can't tell which

2000-2010.what: A glazed veranda with a balcony above was added on the lane-side corner
2000-2010.why: Extension, perhaps for the shop or the family living above it

2000-2010.what: The boards came off its windows and they are open and glazed again
2000-2010.why: Someone reoccupied and repaired the house

2000-2010.what: Its windows, open before, are now boarded up
2000-2010.why: The house was left empty, possibly when its occupant moved (perhaps down to D, timing only, a guess)

2010-2020.what: The big plate-glass shopfront and fascia are gone, replaced by ordinary windows (three on the ground floor, one new at the far left)
2010-2020.why: The shop closed and the ground floor went back to housing

2010-2020.what: Its ground-floor windows gained casings and sills
2010-2020.why: Renewal or repair of the windows, small improvement

A.claim: Built as a large, well-made dwelling with a mansard-type roof and a bay window on the upper floor; roof and upper windows never changed
Its ground floor had already been turned into a shop before 1989 (plate-glass shopfront cut across the original window positions)
It traded as a shop through 1989, 2000 and 2010
Between 2010 and 2020 the shop closed and the shopfront was taken out for regular windows; the house is residential again
Kept in good order throughout, no boarding or damage

B.claim: In 1989 a modest two-storey dwelling with window boxes and a front door with a small canopy
Between 1989 and 2000 its ground floor was converted to a shop (windows replaced by a blank panel, fascia and awning)
Between 2000 and 2010 it was extended with a glazed veranda and a balcony on the lane side
Unchanged and kept from 2010 to 2020; it is the house that kept growing while its neighbours stood still
The blank shop panel has no glazing, so I can't tell if it was trading in 2020

C.claim: A plain, simple house on a stone base beside the landing, with its roof and walls untouched across the whole period
Lived in and kept throughout, never boarded or damaged
Between 2010 and 2020 the owner fitted casings and sills to its ground-floor windows, a modest renewal
Before 1989 it has no visible later additions, so probably a long-standing dwelling kept in its original form

D.claim: Boarded up in 1989 and still boarded in 2000: empty and abandoned for at least eleven years, probably longer
Between 2000 and 2010 the boards were removed and the windows reopened: someone moved in and repaired it
The small lean-to on its side was there already in 1989, so an older addition
Its reopening comes at the same time as E being closed up, so the occupant may have moved from E to D (guess)

E.claim: The small house at the top of the lane was lived in in 1989 and 2000 (windows open, glazed)
Between 2000 and 2010 it was boarded up and left empty
Still boarded in 2020, so vacant for at least ten years
Timing matches D's reopening, so the occupant may have moved down to D (guess)
